title: Nikko — 日光
goal: Understand adult/child person phrases and keep gender separate from family relations.

blocks.text: Nikko is known for its shrines, temples and mountain scenery. Our fictional story uses a group of travellers to practise words for people; it does not ask the learner to guess gender or family relationships from an illustration.
**日光に行きます。** にっこうに いきます。 — I go to Nikko.
**日光で人に会います。** にっこうで ひとに あいます。 — I meet people in Nikko.
The location gives a scene; the formal kanji 男 and 女 complete useful people compounds in the supplied syllabus.

items: **Character:** 日 · **Meaning/reading:** sun/day; にっ in this word · **Radical/components:** 日, ひ · **Status:** Formal review; doubled consonant belongs to the whole word.
**Character:** 光 · **Meaning/reading:** light; コウ, ひかり · **Radical/components:** 儿, にんにょう, below a fire-derived upper shape now resembling ⺌ · **Status:** Assisted encounter; not indexed under 小.

blocks.text: **日光 / にっこう** is the place name. **日光 / にっこう** can also mean sunlight; context distinguishes them. **光 / ひかり — light** is helped vocabulary. The place name is not read にちこう in our course.
**男 / おとこ; 男の人 / おとこのひと — man; 男の子 / おとこのこ — boy.** 男 has radical 田, た, above 力, ちから. Its historical association with work does not prescribe modern occupations or abilities.
**あの男の人は先生です。** あの おとこのひとは せんせいです。 — That man is a teacher.
**男の子がいます。** おとこのこが います。 — There is a boy.
人 gives an adult/person expression; 子 gives the child expression in these words. The noun phrase is not a statement of sibling relationship.
**女 / おんな; 女の人 / おんなのひと — woman; 女の子 / おんなのこ — girl.** 女 is its own radical, おんな; learn its crossing whole shape. In 姉/妹 it appears as the narrower left component おんなへん.
**あの女の人は先生です。** あの おんなのひとは せんせいです。 — That woman is a teacher.
**女の子がいます。** おんなのこが います。 — There is a girl.

These are dictionary meanings for explicitly described fictional people. Names, voices or clothing alone do not establish gender; a question supplies the relevant description if it assesses these words.

cards.title: A person phrase is not a family term

blocks.text: **女の人** means woman; **姉** means the speaker's older sister in our introduction. A woman need not be the speaker's sister, and a boy need not be a younger brother. Likewise 男の子 is not a synonym for 子ども in every sentence; 子ども is broader.
**この女の人は私の姉です。** この おんなのひとは わたしの あねです。 — This woman is my older sister.
The sentence states the relationship explicitly. Without 私の姉, you know only the descriptive noun phrase. Use labels and words, not appearance, as the evidence.
**男の人が二人います。** おとこのひとが ふたり います。 — There are two men.
**女の人が三人います。** おんなのひとが さんにん います。 — There are three women.
**子どもが四人います。** こどもが よにん います。 — There are four children.
These are three separate fictional groups, not an invitation to combine counts unless the question states they are disjoint. Count people with 人, not the general つ counter. 二人 is ふたり, and 四人 is よにん.
**駅に人がいます。** えきに ひとが います。 — There are people at the station.
**駅で姉に会います。** えきで あねに あいます。 — I meet my older sister at the station.
**駅で兄を待ちます。** えきで あにを まちます。 — I wait for my older brother at the station.

Existence, meeting and waiting have different phrase relationships. 人が says who exists; 姉に says whom we meet; 兄を says whom we await. The course does not replace them all with a single “person particle.”
**お寺 / おてら — temple; 神社 / じんじゃ — shrine; 写真 / しゃしん — photograph.** 寺/神/社/写/真 remain helped in this lesson. Spiritual or historical knowledge is not a scored prerequisite.
**お寺の写真を見ます。** おてらの しゃしんを みます。 — I look at a photograph of a temple.
**写真に人がいます。** しゃしんに ひとが います。 — There are people in the photograph.
We use います for the depicted people in this simple scene. Later narrative styles can express what a photo shows in other ways; they are not needed to understand this model.
**姉は先生です。** あねは せんせいです。 — My older sister is a teacher.
**姉は学生でした。** あねは がくせいでした。 — My older sister was a student.
**姉は学生ではありません。** あねは がくせいではありません。 — My older sister is not a student.
These noun descriptions reuse the four polite forms from Package 04. A past identity does not imply that the person has disappeared; it tells you which role is being described at which time.

cards.title: Who is in the picture? dialogue

blocks.text: **A: この人はだれですか。** このひとは だれですか。 — Who is this person?
**B: 私の兄です。** わたしの あにです。 — He is my older brother.
**A: お兄さんは先生ですか。** おにいさんは せんせいですか。 — Is your older brother a teacher?
**B: いいえ、学生です。** いいえ、がくせいです。 — No, he is a student.
The explicit introduction supplies the family relationship. Asking and answering can correct an assumption about a role without changing the basic person phrase.

items: Read 日光, 男の人, 女の子. **Answers:** にっこう; おとこのひと; おんなのこ.
What radical is taught for 光? **Answer:** 儿.
What radical is taught for 男? **Answer:** 田.
Does 女の人 alone mean “my older sister”? **Answer:** No; 姉 expresses that relationship.
Count two people. **Answer:** 二人 / ふたり.
Make 学生です past. **Answer:** 学生でした / がくせいでした.

blocks.text: 日光 is にっこう; 光 is an assisted light character indexed under 儿. 男/女 are formally studied. 男の人/女の人 describe adults; 男の子/女の子 describe children. Family relationship requires its own word or explicit statement. Use 人 to count people and います for their existence.
**Recall:** “There are three women at the station.” **Model:** 駅に女の人が三人います。 えきに おんなのひとが さんにん います。 Next: preferences and skills in 足利.
